answer.evidence: The cart is a wide white tray (rows 3-11, width 16) sitting on a narrower drawer body (rows 12-29, width 14) with small wheels (rows 30-31, width 6). The tray's front edge is a light line at row 10 (#f3f4f7), followed by a darker gray row 11 (#a6a9ad) that acts as eave shadow. The tray interior, with its bottles and items, is visible as an open container (rows 4-9), giving about 7 rows of top surface. The items themselves are drawn face-on, so the top reading is borderline, but the edge line, shadow and visible contents are enough for evidence (d)/(a). Below that is a front face of 18 rows of stacked drawers, each with a handle. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small drawer cart with bottles on top. On the numbers it holds up: 21 visible tones per tile against 17-20 for the stall and well, and 0% near-flat coverage. Structure and shading are weaker. The body is a few flat steps (white, light blue, grey, one dark) with little per-material ramping or grain, against about 5-6 steps on the stall awning and well roof. The outline is a uniform dark line around the whole silhouette, and 91% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, versus 0-1% for the tinted hedge and stall outlines and 33% for the well. The hedge, stall and well use dark material tones and separate forms by value, while this piece reads as a sticker-style outlined sprite. The drawers and bottles are clean, but the shading is shallower and the outline is the near-black type the standard rejects, so it would look flatter next to the stall and well.

The outline is the problem. 91% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the hedge and cheese stall and 33% for the well. The dark grey/black line wraps the whole cart as a uniform sticker outline instead of the dark tone of the adjacent material (dark brown beside wood, dark red-brown beside tiles). The body ramps look shallow, roughly 3-4 steps, on the white/grey frame and the blue drawers. The 21 tones come from many small coloured items (the bottles on top, the drawer handles) rather than from layered shading of the main materials. Because of the near-black outline and the shallower ramps, it would look flatter and more sticker-like beside the references.
